entries.name: input
entries.body: The file or directory to measure. A path given to jint run overrides it.

entries.name: secretDenylist
entries.body: Replaces the built-in denylist of secret-shaped files (gitignore patterns).

entries.name: concurrency
entries.body: The most classifier calls in flight, run-wide, at most 64.

entries.name: timeout
entries.body: The time one classifier call may take, retries included, in seconds. Each attempt gets a third of it.

entries.name: maxInputTokens
entries.body: The most input tokens the model accepts in one call. A call over it is skipped with a note. Unset: elements over 30000 tokens are skipped.

entries.name: charsPerToken
entries.body: The characters of a request's JSON that count as one token, when sizing a call against maxInputTokens. Use a lower number for a model whose tokenizer splits code finely.

entries.name: rules.include
entries.body: The files jint reads, and the default scope of every rule.

entries.name: rules.exclude
entries.body: The files jint skips. Exclude always wins over include.

config.title: Rule fields
config.intro: Each entry of `rules.use` is a rule name or a rule object with these fields.

entries.name: name
entries.body: The rule id: findings join back to it. Two entries with one name are a config error unless the later one sets override.

entries.name: kind
entries.body: The question type. Absent means noul.

entries.name: instructions
entries.body: The yes/no question the model answers, specific to the rule's claim. Required - a generic fallback question would silently recalibrate every classification.

entries.name: criteria
entries.body: The two-sided contract: true names the exact observable condition for yes, false for no. The defect side decides the handle direction.

entries.name: criteria.true
entries.body: The condition for yes.

entries.name: criteria.false
entries.body: The condition for no.

entries.name: target
entries.body: What the rule measures: files, a kind of element, or a capture. A list measures each.

entries.name: handle
entries.body: How a reading becomes a finding. The shape follows the kind of the rule.

entries.name: include
entries.body: Globs of the files this rule reads. It replaces the run include for this rule.

entries.name: exclude
entries.body: Globs of the files this rule skips. Exclude always wins over include.

entries.name: includePath
entries.body: true: the model is handed the file's path with the source. Default false: only the source is sent, so the same code reads the same wherever the file sits. Set it for a rule whose claim is about the path itself.

entries.name: override
entries.body: true: this entry replaces an earlier entry of the same name. Without it a repeated name is a config error, and with it an entry that replaces nothing is too.

config.title: Rule handler fields
config.intro: The `handle` of a rule turns its answer into a severity. The fields it takes depend on the rule kind.

entries.name: map
entries.body: One tier for each score level, in the order of the criteria.

entries.name: map.level
entries.body: The severity of a finding: pass raises none.

entries.name: map.message
entries.body: The rule author's feedback; the finding's note when this tier fires.

entries.name: choices
entries.body: One tier for each option, keyed by the option label.

entries.name: undecided
entries.body: The tier of a reading with no clear winner among the options.

entries.name: undecided.margin
entries.body: The gap between the two likeliest options under which the reading is undecided.

entries.name: undecided.level
entries.body: The severity of a finding: pass raises none.

entries.name: undecided.message
entries.body: The note on the finding of an undecided reading.

entries.name: warn
entries.body: One threshold comparison: exactly one operator. The operator IS the defect direction - greater_than fires on high readings, less_than on low ones. Within (0, 1).

entries.name: warn.greater_than
entries.body: The threshold. A reading above it fires.

entries.name: warn.message
entries.body: The rule author's feedback; the finding's note when this tier fires.

entries.name: warn.less_than
entries.body: The threshold. A reading below it fires.

entries.name: error
entries.body: One threshold comparison: exactly one operator. The operator IS the defect direction - greater_than fires on high readings, less_than on low ones. Within (0, 1).

entries.name: error.greater_than
entries.body: The threshold. A reading above it fires.

entries.name: error.message
entries.body: The rule author's feedback; the finding's note when this tier fires.

entries.name: error.less_than
entries.body: The threshold. A reading below it fires.

entries.name: silent_band
entries.body: A [low, high] range of readings that raises no finding.

entries.name: OPENAI_API_KEY
entries.body: The key for `api.openai.com`. jint sends it nowhere else.

entries.name: JINT_API_URL
entries.body: The endpoint. Its last segment names the wire. See [models and endpoints](../endpoints.md).

entries.name: JINT_API_KEY
entries.body: The key for the url in `JINT_API_URL`. It wins over `OPENAI_API_KEY`.

entries.name: JINT_API_MODEL
entries.body: The model to ask. A `/v1/systemone` server needs it, except TypeSafe's own host.

entries.name: JINT_RUNS_DIR
entries.body: The directory where jint records runs.

entries.name: JINT_CACHE_DIR
entries.body: The directory of the answer cache.

entries.name: JINT_GRAMMAR_DIR
entries.body: The directory of custom grammars.

entries.name: JINT_WALK_WORKERS
pills: the cores available, less one, at most 8, once a run has 64 files to parse
entries.body: The threads that parse files. `1` parses on the main thread; a larger number forces that many threads.

entries.name: JINT_UI_HOST
entries.body: The host that `jint ui serve` binds. Give a host, not `host:port`.

entries.name: JINT_UI_PORT
entries.body: The port that `jint ui serve` binds.

entries.name: JINT_LOG_LEVEL
entries.body: The log level on stderr: `debug`, `info`, `warn`, `error` or `off`.
